answer: Trust moves up to the mobile carrier. Each identity binds to one postpaid line: the carrier sends a signed nonce to the SIM, and the SIM signs it back with a key that never leaves the hardware. The carrier is a wharf where every crate is stamped. The summit of trust sits there, out of cheap reach for fakes. Honest agents get a haven, one line, one identity. An attacker pays real money: 1,000 fakes need 1,000 postpaid lines. At $8 per line per month, that is $8,000 every month, forever, and clustered usage lets the carrier cut all 1,000 lines at once.
